body:
Windows x64 cannot compile the inline x86 assembly used by the shared math helpers, affine transform kernel and collision normalization. Add x64 CPUID, prefetch and SSE intrinsic paths while retaining the existing Win32 implementations and Linux paths. The affine kernel preserves operation grouping, zero-lane additions and read-before-write alias behavior; normalization applies SQRTSS to the existing rounded float input before the existing reciprocal.

Four production files, +235/−1, directly above upstream `master`. The source delta and final source blobs match the independently reviewed master-based package; the source has no CI-code dependency. This source change does not depend on the FPU control package or the LP64 history.

The [recorded v120 evidence](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/4849c510c4983fd00a0515bc309a133090ffb7ab/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/math-native-results.md) comes from client counterpart translation units and client dependencies, not a Windows server build. The SSE additions match the client additions; the existing server Transform/CollisionUtils files have other baseline differences, so whole-file hashes differ.

- **Transform:** 1,024 cases per Debug/Release run; all 768 finite cases and the tested alias/control cases match across ABIs. Debug matches throughout. Release retains 464 NaN-payload word differences in 136 exceptional records and a failed strict comparator.
- **Collision:** 8,192 sampled values, line-twist classifications and MXCSR words match per configuration using PC64 Win32, aligned rounding controls and DAZ off. The separately recorded x87 status has no x64 counterpart. The four successful sharedCollision builds are client builds.
- **SseMath:** the [native Win32 register-clobber diagnosis](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/4849c510c4983fd00a0515bc309a133090ffb7ab/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/ssemath-clobber-analysis.md) explains why the arithmetic comparison uses a separately named diagnostic reload control. In 33,280 records per configuration, finite/subnormal/extreme/discarded-lane categories agree with the historical x64 candidate; exceptional differences remain. The original result recorded source `701111df…`, while this package contains `7d23411f…`. A bounded follow-up compiled and linked that exact client counterpart source/header in v120 Debug/x64 and Release/x64; each 33,280-record output is byte-identical to its original candidate oracle. This qualifies the sampled client counterpart, not the server dependency closure.

For the Windows math qualification, only the two source-identity checks above were added during packaging; original flags, inputs and oracle were unchanged. Two collector-only parsing errors before execution are retained. Each probe ran once; no full Windows client/server build was repeated. Corrected input probes avoid the Win32 x87 float-return conversion seen in earlier signaling-NaN fixtures. Existing results do not establish general NaN-payload or signed-zero equivalence, normal dispatch/gameplay behavior, exception delivery, or a complete Windows server build.

[Source identities, independent review and exact-source native check](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/bbbfeae1c2e9b0adb979fd29ca5f501608fe5512/review/client-x64/pr-ready-next/server-math-kernels/RESULTS.md).

The CI commits include the [existing workflow repair (#38)](https://github.com/SWG-Source/src/pull/38) and a manual qualification trigger. They check out the submitted head and build it in the pinned legacy container instead of invoking the broken bare-repository clone. The earlier failed upstream checks remain visible. No production file changed when adding this repair.

[Full legacy Linux32 build on this head](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/src/actions/runs/36899818839) passed at `8931a807e135b72897105c82c9576b7795f5d081`, including the tracked-input integrity check. This checks the Linux configuration; it does not compile or execute the Windows-only paths described above.
